# Psalm 144 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** By David. Praise the LORD, my rock! He trains my hands for battle and my fingers for fighting.

**2** He is my loving ally and my fortress, my tower of safety and my rescuer, my shield and my shelter. He brings nations under my authority.

**3** LORD, what are human beings that you even notice them? What are mortals that you think about them?

**4** People are like a puff of air; their days pass like a fleeting shadow.

**5** LORD, rip open the sky and come down! Touch the mountains and make them erupt in smoke!

**6** Hurl your lightning bolts and scatter the enemy; shoot your arrows and throw them into chaos!

**7** Reach down from heaven and pull me out! Rescue me from this flood of enemies — from these foreigners

**8** whose mouths are full of lies and who raise their right hands to swear false oaths.

**9** God, I will sing a brand-new song to you! I will make music on a ten-stringed harp,

**10** to the God who gives kings their victories, who rescues his servant David from the deadly sword.

**11** Save me! Rescue me from these lying foreigners whose mouths are full of deceit and whose handshakes mean nothing.

**12** Then our sons will flourish like well-nurtured plants in their youth; our daughters will be like graceful pillars carved to adorn a palace.

**13** Our barns will be bursting with every kind of crop; our sheep will multiply by the thousands — tens of thousands in our fields.

**14** Our cattle will be fat and healthy; there will be no breach in the walls, no exile, and no cries of alarm in our streets.

**15** How blessed are the people who have all this! How blessed are the people whose God is the LORD!

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **144:15**: The psalm's last line says it all: material blessings are wonderful — 'but blessed are the people whose God is the LORD.' The real blessing isn't stuff; it's who your God is.

— PNEUMA
